content:
Donald Trump will make it rain pardons before leaving the White House, “Late Night” host Seth Meyers and MS NOW’s Chris Hayes predicted on Monday.

During an interview on Meyers’ show, the comedian suggested Trump may soon begin worrying about “the legality of what he’s done in office, the people around him, certainly as people start investigating possible corruption.”

He then asked Hayes for his “over-under number of pardons” Trump might issue before his presidency ends. “I’m gonna give you a real number because I’m not joking around,” Meyers said, before putting his estimate at 2,000.

“Wow,” Hayes replied, saying he’d “probably take the over.”

“I think it’s gonna be over, too. I think it’s gonna be nuts,” Meyers agreed.

Hayes pointed to previous presidents issuing pardons covering entire groups of people, including Jimmy Carter’s pardon of Vietnam War draft evaders and Trump’s sweeping clemency for Jan. 6 defendants.

He then pondered whether Trump could declare that no Republican officeholder could be prosecuted for federal crimes. Trump “loves that power and, on the way out, is going to absolutely maximally employ it,” he said.

“I think it’s going to be so far over 2,000,” Meyers concluded.
